text:
Whether to rent or buy depends more on how long you will stay than on ideology. Closing costs run 2-5% of the purchase price, and selling means paying agent commissions too. So a buyer who expects to move within roughly five years usually loses money. Early mortgage payments go mostly to interest, and equity builds slowly.

The local market also gives a signal. A price-to-rent ratio above about 20 favors renting, and a ratio below 15 favors buying.

First-time buyers often take the largest loan a lender will approve. Many then find that owning has its own ongoing costs: maintenance alone takes 1-2% of the home's value each year. A 20% down payment avoids private mortgage insurance.

Test the results of any rent-versus-own calculator against how likely you are to change jobs and move. Think of a house as shelter first and an investment second: the roof matters more than the return. Renters who diligently invest the money they save often end up with a net worth similar to owners'.
